analysis.evidence: וַיִּסַּע narrates Abram’s departure. The following infinitives הָלוֹךְ וְנָסוֹעַ describe his continued travel, and הַנֶּגְבָּה gives its direction, toward the Negev.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with אַבְרָם as its subject. The initial נ of the root assimilates to ס, marked by the dagesh.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּסַּע אַבְרָם, Abram is the subject of the singular verb וַיִּסַּע, “he set out.” The verse describes his journey toward the Negev.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67589:2, 67587:4.
נָסוֹעַ repeats the verb וַיִּסַּע. Together, הָלוֹךְ וְנָסוֹעַ portray Abram’s travel as continuing, and הַנֶּגְבָּה gives its direction, toward the Negev.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the Qal infinitive absolute נָסוֹעַ to the preceding infinitive absolute הָלוֹךְ.
analysis.sense: journey on, move from place to place

analysis.evidence: הָלוֹךְ וְנָסוֹעַ describes Abram’s continued journey. The article identifies the Negev as the region, and the directional ending marks it as the goal of travel.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun. Final ה marks direction, with the ending pronounced ־ָה.
